chunks: As for what Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

One does not perform salat over the newborn, and he is the child who did not cry out, did not give a sound, and is not inherited from in the blood-money nor from anything else. But if he cried out, then perform salat over him and give him inheritance.

So the proper way to understand this narration is that it indicates a kind of recommendation, according to what we mentioned earlier, or dissimulation (taqiyyah), in accordance with what the first report contained; and this confirms what we have said.

key_terms.يَسْتَهِلَّ: to cry out at birth as a sign of life
key_terms.يُصَلِّي: to perform funeral salat over the deceased
key_terms.يُوَرَّثْ: to be given inheritance rights or to inherit
key_terms.ٱلتَّقِيَّةُ: dissimulation for protection in a context of legal expression
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةِ: blood-money compensation connected here to inheritance rulings
key_terms.ٱلْمَنْفُوسِ: the newborn infant being discussed in the ruling

ai.seo_question: Is salat performed over a newborn who dies before crying out or showing signs of life?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of salat over a newborn who dies before showing signs of life. It distinguishes between a stillborn child who never cried out and one who did, linking that distinction to funeral prayer and inheritance, while the compiler clarifies that the report is to be understood as recommendation or taqiyyah.
